terms.comment: Egger’s phrase, a “mark of descent”, the first that Morgan–Owens gives. The adjective geneticus, genetica, geneticum (genetic) is modern too, made on Greek γενετικός; genetics is genetica or doctrīna genetica (M-O s.v. genetics).

evidence: M-O s.v. gene (Helfer; Lexicon recentis Latinitatis)
terms.comment: A short coinage on the modern languages’ word; Morgan–Owens marks it as less recommended than Egger’s phrase.

classical.html: Classical Latin speaks of inheritance through the parents and nature: what a child takes from them is ā parentibus acceptum or ā patre, and a family likeness lies in the stirps or genus. These say “it runs in the family”, not “gene”.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.vv. gene, genetic, genetics.
No classical source, nor Traupman nor Levi & Bini, has a word for a gene.
